clue.text: Those who should be inside out

definitions.text: Those who should be inside out

parts.words: Those who should be inside out
parts.note: surface reading: people who ought to be indoors, perhaps sheltering; setter's reading: 'inside' is slang for in prison, and these people should be there but are out

explanation.surface: Someone scolding those who ought to stay indoors but have gone outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside out' looks like the phrase for a garment turned over; split it, and 'inside' means in jail while 'out' means at large.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners who have broken free belong in jail yet are at liberty, which is exactly the paradox described.

clue.text: They should be able to identify any salts in a mixture

definitions.text: They should be able to identify any salts in a mixture
definitions.note: plural 'They' for a singular noun: the clue thinks of individual tests

parts.words: identify any salts in a mixture
parts.note: surface reading: the words invite an anagram of 'any salts', which does not quite work; setter's reading: chemical testing reveals which salts a sample contains

explanation.surface: A description of chemists' tests for finding salts in a compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Any salts' and 'mixture' tempt an anagram, but those letters hold a T and no I; the clue is a straight description of chemical testing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical examination of a sample determines its constituent substances, such as the salts present.

clue.text: Highlight of 70s' fashion trousers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bright signal light, a flash that lights up

definitions.note: describes one leg of a pair of flares rather than naming a noun directly
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the singular of the bell-bottom trousers popular in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Asking whether bell-bottoms were the high point of seventies style.
explanation.walkthrough: Flares were wide-bottomed trousers fashionable in the 1970s; the question mark admits the singular is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyrotechnic signal lights things up, and the widening leg of such trousers shares the name.

clue.text: Phaeton's rebuilt as a carriage for one

indicators.note: something rebuilt is taken apart and put together again in a new form

parts.note: the possessive supplies an extra S to the fodder

explanation.surface: A phaeton, an open horse-drawn coach, being remodelled into a single-seater.
explanation.walkthrough: A phaeton is itself a horse-drawn carriage, which makes the surface seamless.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light open horse-drawn vehicle seating a single person, named after the clergyman it was built for.

clue.text: Where teachers teach?

parts.note: surface reading: asking for the classroom or the school; setter's reading: the answer split in two says where (in a class), and read whole is a verb meaning tell or instruct

explanation.surface: A simple question about the place where lessons happen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, it is 'in form', a form being a British school class; read as one, it is what teachers do.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell or give knowledge to someone is what educators do, and a form is a school class.

clue.text: Many cheer the reformation of Satan

indicators.note: a reformation remakes something into a different shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Crowds celebrate as the Devil turns over a new leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is the chief foe of God and humankind, the supreme adversary in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Sun-god took men to the moon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Greek god of the sun, music and poetry

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the space programme that did it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the NASA programme whose missions landed astronauts on the lunar surface

explanation.surface: A mythical deity ferrying people from the sun to the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of light gave his name to the American space missions that achieved lunar landings.

clue.text: Barmaids need not give change for these machines

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all three words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Bar staff are told they needn't supply coins for the pub's fruit machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give change' reads as handing out coins, which suits gambling machines, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Slot machines are nicknamed this because of their single lever and the way they take players' money.

clue.text: The only one in a suit wearing a vest

definitions.text: The only one in a suit

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
clothes you are wearing are on you

explanation.surface: Someone sporting a vest as the only person in a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge and whist, this is a lone card of its suit in a hand; 'wearing a vest' becomes 'vest on', in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Card players use the term for a hand holding just one card of a particular suit.

clue.text: Mature, or mature to a point

parts.note: fruit that is mature is ready to eat
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between letting a thing age naturally or aging it until it peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word looks like a double definition; the second 'mature' is an adjective followed by a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to full development, as fruit does when it becomes ready to eat.

clue.text: A new role in flight control

indicators.note: making something new gives it a fresh form, so the letters around it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone taking up a fresh job in air traffic control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A new role' reads as one phrase, but 'new' sits inside the fodder, which also takes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: This hinged flap on an aircraft wing controls roll, so it is a control surface for flying.

clue.text: Shattered hope and returning trouble robbed her of the will to live

definitions.text: robbed her of the will to live
definitions.note: a description of the woman this happened to, not a noun naming her

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into fragments that can be put back in another order

parts.note: used letter for letter

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Despair and misfortune drive a woman to give up on life.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine of Shakespeare's Hamlet, driven mad, drowns; the whole clue narrates her fate while the first half builds her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to Hamlet's beloved, whose grief and madness lead to her drowning in the play.

clue.text: A piece of cake for a midshipman

definitions.note: a noun standing for a character's surname
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the hero of Captain Marryat's novel Mr Midshipman ___

explanation.surface: Offering a slice of cake to a junior naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is an 1836 sea novel by Frederick Marryat; 'a piece of cake' is idiom, not a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no trouble at all is idiomatically a piece of cake, and the novel's young officer bears this surname.

clue.text: Open and confined spaces for relaxation in school

definitions.note: describes the place by its purpose rather than naming it

parts.note: a common is an open stretch of public land
a room is an enclosed space within walls

explanation.surface: A school providing both outdoor and indoor areas where pupils can unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: A common is a village's shared open grassland, a very British feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Schools and colleges have a lounge shared by staff or students for resting between lessons.

clue.text: Girl and boy flirted

parts.note: Carrie is a girl's name
Don is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young couple trading glances and teasing each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a dalliance or affair with someone is idiomatically to have gone on with them in that way.

clue.text: Fall of rotter in lawsuit

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, enclosed on both sides

parts.note: a case is a legal action brought in court
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's downfall in a court action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' reads as a downfall, but it is a waterfall; rotter and cad are old British words for a cad's sort of man.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall, especially one tumbling in stages over rocks, is a falling torrent of water.

clue.text: It may identify the member leading the orchestra

indicators.note: one thing leading another goes in front of it in the line

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A badge marking out the principal player at the head of an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The member leading the orchestra' sounds like the first violinist; it is a limb placed before a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth worn on the sleeve can mark the wearer's role, such as a team captain or steward.

clue.text: Opening for a photographer

parts.note: surface reading: a job vacancy or opportunity for someone who takes pictures; setter's reading: the literal hole in a camera lens that lets the light in

explanation.surface: A job advertisement inviting applications from photographers.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjustable hole in a camera lens controls how much light reaches the film or sensor.

clue.text: Runners allowed to enter various heats

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is put within another
various suggests different arrangements, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: used letter for letter
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Racers being permitted to compete in several qualifying rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heats' and 'Runners' share the athletics scene, so 'heats' looks like part of the definition, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Track competitors who race are sportspeople, so runners are one kind of these sportspeople.

clue.text: Soldiers in irregular wars need someone to provide intelligence

indicators.note: one thing in another sits within it, surrounded on both sides
irregular means out of the usual order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: used letter for letter
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Guerrilla conflicts require troops to gather military intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' looks like spying, but here it is simply news; the anagram fodder includes 'need'.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who reads out bulletins on radio or TV supplies information, an older sense of the word.

clue.text: Call for action put out by the Salvation Army

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rallying shout before battle

definitions.text: put out by the Salvation Army
definitions.note: describes the publication by its publisher
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the title of the Salvation Army's weekly newspaper

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army issuing a summons to its members to act.
explanation.walkthrough: The Salvation Army, a Christian charity organised on military lines, publishes a paper called The War Cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout used to rally fighters, and also the name of the charity's long-running weekly publication.

clue.text: A disposition of arms

parts.note: surface reading: the deployment of weapons or troops; setter's reading: the human limbs, held in a particular pose

explanation.surface: A military description of how weapons are positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing with hands on hips and elbows turned outwards is a particular posture of the upper limbs.

clue.text: How about a call to slow down?

indicators.note: about suggests turning around and moving letters into a different order

parts.note: used letter for letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider wondering whether to shout for the horse to ease up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How about' reads as a suggestion; here 'about' acts on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders shout this to a horse to make it stop, and it is used generally to tell someone to ease up.

clue.text: Climbing gear?

parts.note: surface reading: ropes, harnesses and other mountaineering equipment; setter's reading: the car gear a driver selects to go up a steep hill

explanation.surface: Asking about equipment for mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest ratio in a car gearbox gives the most pulling power, so drivers use it on steep inclines.

clue.text: Airs composed by priest in Hebrew

indicators.note: something composed is put together or arranged, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: used letter for letter
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: Melodies written by a cleric in the Hebrew language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' sits naturally with 'airs' as music writing, but signals the anagram; Eli is crosswords' stock priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish person, or a citizen of the modern Jewish state, can be loosely called a Hebrew.

clue.text: Become weak, get nurse round for the final stage

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it on every side

parts.note: to tend is to nurse or look after
to ail is to grow sick or feeble

explanation.surface: Someone growing frail and needing a carer towards the end of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The last part of something, such as a queue or an innings, is its rear or concluding portion.

clue.text: Roots develop into a trunk

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so these letters grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tree's roots growing up into its trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about trees, but this trunk is the human body's.
explanation.definitionFit: The main part of the human body, excluding head and limbs, is also called the trunk.

clue.text: Soup ingredient often includes eggs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the swiftlet nests used in a Chinese delicacy soup

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the home a bird builds, which usually holds its clutch

explanation.surface: A recipe note about a soup containing eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiftlets make nests of saliva that are prized in Chinese cooking for a famous soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible swiftlet nests flavour a Chinese delicacy, and an ordinary avian nest usually holds a clutch.
